highlight.title: Meet Mira, your AI assistant
highlight.description: Ask questions about your scenarios in plain language and get answers computed from your actual data, without digging through tables yourself. Once Mira is enabled for an app, open it with the Mira button in the header.
highlight.mediaAlt: Video: Meet Mira, the AI assistant in GAMS MIRO 2.14

features.title: Ask about your data
features.text: Analyze the sandbox scenario or a comparison of scenarios: which routes changed the most, which inputs look off, what drove the result.

features.title: Change inputs in plain language
features.text: Ask, e.g., "increase demand in the EU by 10%", review the before/after preview and apply it with one click.

features.title: Charts in answers
features.text: Mira adds charts to its answers. The data is read from the scenario database by MIRO, never written by the model, and every chart opens in the pivot comparison view.

features.title: Help in Configuration Mode
features.text: Get assistance writing custom renderers.

highlight.note: Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Microsoft Foundry and Amazon Bedrock. On MIRO Desktop, Mira can also use any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible server, such as a company AI gateway or a locally running model.

major: New, modern design for MIRO apps, MIRO Desktop and MIRO Server.

Scenario comparison: Select one of the loaded scenarios as baseline. In the pivot view, views are taken from the baseline scenario, and the new record _baseline compares against it in MIRO Pivot and dashboards. The sandbox scenario is no longer included automatically; include it explicitly when loading scenarios. Custom and dashboard comparison modules can enable baseline selection via selectBaseline.
MIRO Desktop: Edit environment variables directly in the settings window; exporting and importing them is no longer necessary.

MIRO Desktop for Linux now bundles R and all required R packages, so there's no need to install R or compilers separately or wait for packages to compile on first launch. An RPM package is also available for Fedora and RHEL.
MIRO Desktop updates can now be installed directly from Help → Check for Update on Windows, macOS and Linux (AppImage). Automatic update checks are optional, and installation requires confirmation.
minor: Baseline comparisons: In MIRO Pivot and dashboards, a record missing in one of the scenarios now counts as 0 if the aggregation function is sum or count (GAMS does not store zeros). Previously, such values were left empty.
Numerical tolerance: A global threshold below which values are treated as zero in baseline comparisons, avoiding inflated percentages caused by floating-point noise.
Hide symbols in comparisons: Hide specific input/output symbols in split, tab and pivot comparison mode while still showing them everywhere else.
MIRO Pivot: The thresholds at which data is truncated before rendering (e.g., maximum number of chart data points, pie slices or table columns) are configurable.
MIRO Pivot: Option to hide the chart legend in views.
Custom theme colors: The main background color can now also be set for light mode, and the highlighted sidebar entry stays readable on dark sidebars.
Attachments: Option to prevent attachments from overwriting model files.
Background tasks: Smoother job submission, progress tracking and result downloads without interrupting your workflow.
MIRO Server: If a user has no default scenario of their own, the one of the user who added or last updated the app is loaded, normally the scenario bundled with the app.
Documentation: New design and layout with clearer guides, improved navigation and search, and light/dark theme support.
